# De Dolle Brouwers

> Family-run craft brewery in Esen (Diksmuide), West Flanders, Belgium, brewing since 1980. Known for Oerbier, Arabier, Boskeun, Dulle Teve and Stille Nacht. Taproom (the Oerbar) open on weekends, brewery tour every Sunday, merchandise sold online. Official website: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be (the old site oerbier.be is no longer maintained).

Key facts:

- Address: Roeselarestraat 12B, 8600 Esen (Diksmuide), Belgium
- Email: info@dedollebrouwers.be
- Oerbar (taproom): Saturday and Sunday, 14:00–19:00
- Getting there: by car, or by train to Diksmuide (the station is 4 km from the brewery, where electric shared bikes from Hoppy can be taken through an app). Nearby: IJzertoren and Dodengang in Diksmuide, Veurne, Ieper and the coast.
- Brewery tour: every Sunday, 14:00 in English and 15:00 in Dutch; about 45 minutes, includes three tastings from the cask; €10 per person; book and pay online, or buy a ticket on the spot while there is room. No tours during the Christmas closure (22 December – 18 January). Groups of 20 or more can ask for a separate tour by email.
- Beer is not sold in the webshop: buy it in the Oerbar or at the bars and shops on the "where to drink" map.
- Webshop (merchandise): hoodies, crewnecks, T-shirts, a cap, the Oerbier figure (also personalised), metal signs, a set of six posters, glasses, a hand-drawn €50 gift voucher (sent by post), the book Hidden Beers of Belgium and Garbage Pail Kids Taste Buds packs (Kris is card 2a, "Crafted Kris"). Shipping to most of Europe, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and Canada, and (until 15 January 2027, after which new US customs rules apply) the United States; import duties for the US are paid at checkout. Free pick-up in the Oerbar.

Full text of the main pages below (English). Short version: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/llms.txt. Generated from the live site, so check the page itself for the latest.

# Visit the brewery and the Oerbar
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/visit

Roeselarestraat 12B, Esen

## Come and visit.
A brewery from 1835, equipment more than a hundred years old that still runs on every brew day, and a bar full of beer brewed right here. Every Sunday we give a brewery tour, and on weekends the Oerbar, our taproom, is open.
Book a tour
Saturday
Oerbar 2 – 7 pm

Sunday
Oerbar 2 – 7 pm · Tour 2 pm (English) & 3 pm (Dutch)

Price
€10 per person, with three tastings from the cask

Closed during the Christmas holidays. Check our socials before you come.

### What to expect.
Plan for an afternoon ↓

- 1

#### Brewery tour
Forty-five minutes through the brewhouse, past the malt mill, the mash tun and the open fermenters. With stories you won't hear anywhere else.

- 2

#### The coolship
The coolship dates from 1921, when the brewery was rebuilt after the First World War, and is still in use: every brew cools down here. There aren't many breweries left where you can still see that.

- 3

#### The Oerbar
After the tour you taste three beers from the cask. Then you can order the whole range in our taproom, including Oeral, which you can only drink here, and the Reservas, which are hard to find in other bars.

- 4

#### The terrace
In good weather you sit outside, between the old brewery buildings, with a De Dolle Brouwers beer in the sun.

### Practical.

#### Sunday brewery tour
At 2 pm in English and at 3 pm in Dutch. About 45 minutes, €10 per person, including three tastings from the cask. Book online or just turn up and buy a ticket on the spot.
Book your spot

#### Coming with a group?
For 20 people or more we plan a separate tour, also on weekdays. Email info@dedollebrouwers.be .

#### How to find us
Roeselarestraat 12B, 8600 Esen, Belgium. Just outside Diksmuide, not far from the coast. You can come by car, or by train to Diksmuide: the station is 4 km from the brewery. There you can take an electric shared bike (Hoppy) through the app, from €1 an hour.
Directions in Google Maps ↗

#### Combine it with the Westhoek
A Sunday at the brewery fits nicely into a day out nearby:

- IJzertoren (Yser Tower) and Dodengang (Trench of Death) in Diksmuide. The trench is about 1.5 km from the tower, on the Yser. It is closed in winter (1 December to mid-February), so check the opening hours first.
- Veurne. For its Grote Markt (main square).
- Ieper. For the Menin Gate and the In Flanders Fields Museum.
- The coast, Nieuwpoort or De Panne. Not far away, before or after your tour.

More questions? Read the FAQ or get in touch .

Tour at 2 pm (English) or 3 pm (Dutch). After that, the Oerbar is all yours.

# FAQ
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/faq

Frequently asked questions

## Everything you want to know before you come.
Question not listed? Feel free to email info@dedollebrouwers.be .

Do I need to book a tour in advance? No need. For the Sunday tour (2 pm English, 3 pm Dutch) you can book here on the site , or just turn up and buy a ticket on the spot. Coming with a big group on a Sunday? Please let us know beforehand.
Can I bring my dog? Dogs are always welcome here, in the Oerbar and on the terrace. There are pretty much always a few dogs around. Only during the brewery tour they can't come along.
Can children come along? Children are welcome in the Oerbar and on the terrace. The tour itself goes through a working brewery with stairs and narrow passages, so keep that in mind with young children.
How can I pay in the Oerbar? Cash or with Payconiq.
We're coming with a large group — is that possible? Groups of 20 or more are booked by appointment, also on weekdays. Email info@dedollebrouwers.be with the date you'd like and the size of your group, and we'll see what's possible.
Can I buy beer to take home? Yes, in the Oerbar you can buy bottles of the whole range, including the Reserva beers while stocks last. You'll also find our glasses and merchandise, like hoodies, T-shirts, caps and the Oerbier figure. Handy if you're looking for a nice gift, for Father's Day for example.
Are tours available in English? Absolutely. Every Sunday there's a tour at 2 pm in English and at 3 pm in Dutch. Lots of international visitors come to the brewery.

# Our story
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/our-story

## From cycling club to brewery.
In 1980 Kris Herteleer founded De Dolle Brouwers together with his brother Jo and two friends from the little cycling club De Dolle Dravers. They weren't complete beginners: for three years they had practised at home, in a copper washtub over a wood fire. With the empty brewery in Esen, that hobby suddenly became serious. The name of their cycling club inspired the name of the brewery: De Dolle Brouwers (the mad brewers).

Nat en straf, from the very start

- 1835 Doctor Louis Nevejan founds a brewery with a distillery in Esen. The village has six of them at the time.

- 1882 The Costenoble family takes over: Brouwerij Sint-Henricus. They brew there for three generations, mostly oud bruin. In the early '80s the brewery falls silent.

- 1921 After the First World War the brewery is rebuilt. We still use the copper coolship from that time today.

- 1955 Trappist beer is brewed at the brewery.

- '70 A little cycling club, “De Dolle Dravers”: the brothers Jo and Kris Herteleer, Dirk Coussée and Bernard Veranneman. They know every hill, and every café.

- 1980 After test brews in the washtub they take over the empty brewery. On 15 November they brew the first Oerbier.

- 1996 The first beer goes into wine barrels to age.

- 2000 Stille Nacht Reserva 2000 becomes the first Reserva, in red Bordeaux barrels. Since then there have been three: Oerbier, Dulle Teve and Stille Nacht Reserva.

- Now About 1,200 hectolitres a year. Small enough to keep an eye on everything ourselves.

### From the photo album.
20 April 1990

### Everything drawn by hand.
Labels, posters, characters: Kris Herteleer has drawn them himself from the very start. That's why you can spot a De Dolle Brouwers beer from afar.

More work by Kris ↗

# How we brew
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/brewing

The Oerbier figure explains ↘

## How we brew. Since 1980.
Ten steps from grain to bottle. Nothing filtered, nothing pasteurised, and with equipment more than a hundred years old that is still in use, like the mash tun and the coolship.
Start at step 1 ↓

Step 1 + malt

### Malt
It all starts with malted barley. Sack by sack the malt goes into the hopper, on its way to the mill.

Step 2

### Milling
Our old malt mill cracks the grains open, so the starch inside can do its work. That faithful machine has been running here for decades.
The real one, still in service

Step 3 + water

### Mashing
The milled malt goes into the mash tun with water from our own wells. We rest it at 63 °C and then at 73 °C, so the enzymes turn the starch into sugars. Then we filter off the sweet wort . The mash tun is probably even older than the coolship.
Mash tun no. 1, still in use

Step 4 + Belgian hop cones

### Boiling
The wort comes to the boil in the brew kettle. In go the Belgian hop cones: for bitterness, aroma and natural protection.

Step 5 90°

### The coolship
The hot wort, still around 90 °C, flows into our coolship : a wide, open copper tray. Copper, just like our fermenters. Here it rests while the sediment settles. The coolship dates from 1921, when the brewery was rebuilt after the First World War, and still does its job.
Wort in the coolship

Step 6 ↓ 25°

### The Baudelot cooler
Then it runs over the pipes of our Baudelot cooler, with cold running water, and drops to about 25 °C. Just right for the yeast.
The Baudelot cooler (don't touch!)

Step 7 + yeast

### Fermentation
In our open copper vessels our own house yeast gets to work. It turns the sugars into alcohol and CO₂. A big part of what makes a De Dolle Brouwers beer so distinctive.
Open fermentation, for real

Step 8 4° · 2 months

### Maturing
After fermentation the beer rests for at least two months in the lagering tanks, at 4 °C. We take our time: that's where the flavours round off.

Step 9 + sugar & yeast

### Bottling
Before bottling we add a little sugar and fresh yeast. Then every bottle is filled and capped.
Our bottling machine

Step 10

### The warm room
The crates go to the warm room, where the beer referments in the bottle. That's how every De Dolle Brouwers beer gets its natural sparkle.

An extra step, sometimes

### And then a year in the barrel.
Now and then a batch of Oerbier, Dulle Teve or Stille Nacht doesn't go into the bottle after fermentation but into old wine barrels. It stays there for at least a year, sometimes much longer. We have been ageing beer in wine barrels since 1996. The first Reserva was Stille Nacht Reserva 2000, in red Bordeaux barrels.
To the Reservas

### Santé!
Rather see it for yourself? Every Sunday Kris takes you through the brewery, with three tastings from the cask.
2 pm English 3 pm Dutch
Book a tour

# Oerbier
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/oerbier

← All beers

9%

Our first beer, since 1980

## Oerbier

- 9%
- Dark, top-fermented
- Refermented in the bottle The very first beer of the brewery, officially brewed since 15 November 1980. Seven kinds of malt, a complex yeast and whole-cone hops from Poperinge. Unfiltered and refermented in the bottle.

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Rich, yeasty and darkly malty, with a light fruity touch.

Taste
Rich, complex flavours in balance. The sweet malt has the upper hand, with lightly hoppy, bitter and slightly sour notes.

Finish
Full-bodied and floral.

In the glass
The poster

#### Serving tip
Keep cool and dark in the cellar and pour at 12°C into the Oerbier glass or a wine glass.

#### Keeping
Keeps for at least two years, but Oerbier keeps evolving and can be cellared much longer.

#### Did you know...

- De Dolle Brouwers started out as De Dolle Dravers, a cycling club with four members.
- Oerbier was perfected over three years in a copper washtub over a wood fire.
- At a blind tasting in the Brouwershuis it came out as the best.
- The year 1980 refers to the first official brew, on 15 November 1980. It was the start of a revival of special beers in Belgium.
- Take a good look at the logo on the glass: it's not a lady, a monk or a king, but a personified yeast cell.
- After a few years of ageing Oerbier takes on a wine-like character.
- The brewery still keeps samples of the very first brew, and they are still perfectly drinkable.
- "Nat en straf" (wet and strong) on the glasses is a warning about the 9%.
- The Oerbier figure holds a brewer's fork, the work, but looks at the glass of beer, the result.
- On the metal signs the Oerbier figure rides a wild beast, after the cave drawings of Altamira in Spain, from around 15,000 BC.

### More of our beers

- Arabier 8%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Boskeun 9%
- Dulle Teve 10% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Arabier
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/arabier

← All beers

8%

The blond sister of Oerbier

## Arabier

- 8%
- Blond, dry-hopped
- Refermented in the bottle Plenty of beer lovers liked Oerbier, but also asked for a pale beer. So came Arabier: brewed with a single malt, pale malt, and a bitterness that keeps the taste in balance.

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Fruity, fresh and bitter, from the WGV hops (Whitbread Golding Variety).

Taste
Dry and fresh, with a Nugget hop bitterness that balances the pale malt.

Finish
Long and bitter, refreshing to the last sip.

In the glass
The poster

#### Serving tip
Drink Arabier cool, at 10 °C, as it says in Arabic on the bottle.

#### Keeping
Keeps for two years; the date is on the crown cap.

#### Did you know...

- Beer is beer, but it had to start with an A. So Arabier it was: ideal after an afternoon walking in the desert.
- The label shows a colourful parrot, a macaw ("ara" in Dutch).
- The bottle says in Arabic: "Drink cool, 10 °C".
- The hop cones grow around Poperinge. They are dried, pressed and added to the wort like that.
- In Dutch the name is always written with a small a.
- One arabier, two arabiers. But there are never two Arabs ("arabieren").
- A wink: in Arab countries beer is actually forbidden.

### More of our beers

- Oerbier 9%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Boskeun 9%
- Dulle Teve 10% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Boskeun
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/boskeun

← All beers

9%

One of the first Easter beers

## Boskeun

- 9%
- Easter beer
- Refermented in the bottle Our Easter beer of 9%, following Stille Nacht in the year. The unique ingredient is honey, one of the oldest sweeteners for drinks. Soft in taste, with a fruity aroma.

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Fruity, with a touch of honey.

Taste
Soft, with the round sweetness of the honey.

Finish
Long and soft.

In the glass
The poster

#### Serving tip
Pour it into the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

#### Did you know...

- Easter beer has been a thing in Belgium only since 1982. Before that there was just the Easter beer of Slaghmuylder, a stronger pils.
- "Boskeun" is West Flemish for wild rabbit. A rabbit is cuddly, sweet and soft.
- Brewed with pale malt, Golding hops from Poperinge, organic cane sugar, honey and pure spring water.
- Honey is one of the oldest sweeteners for drinks.
- Unfiltered, unpasteurised and refermented in the bottle.
- "Keun" was the nickname of Jo, one of the Herteleer brothers. After a brotherly fight he was left with a cut on his upper lip, a hare lip. That is how it became Boskeun.

### A new Boskeun every spring
We brew Boskeun once a year, for Easter. And every year Benjamin Herteleer, the youngest generation of the family, draws a new picture for it: the Boskeun rabbits in their underground local, at the Easter table or around a campfire in the woods, with a pot of honey of course. The batch usually sells out fast. Want to know when the new brew is in? Keep an eye on our socials: @dedollebrouwers .

### More of our beers

- Oerbier 9%
- Arabier 8%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Dulle Teve 10% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Dulle Teve
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/dulle-teve

← All beers

10%

Our tripel, with a story

## Dulle Teve

- 10%
- Tripel
- Refermented in the bottle A golden tripel of 10%, brewed with white candi sugar in the kettle. The name was born in the Oerbar, when an impatient landlady snapped at her husband on the phone: "Do you know what you are? A dulle teve!" (a mad bitch) — and the brewers knew at once: name found, now we just have to brew the beer.

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Fruity, with a touch of candi sugar.

Taste
Full, with the sweetness of the white candi sugar.

Finish
Long and dry, with the 10% well hidden.

The poster

#### Serving tip
Pour at 10°C into the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

#### When
Available almost all year round.

#### Keeping
Best in a cool cellar.

#### Did you know...

- "Dulle teve" is dialect for a difficult woman.
- The café owner who phoned was looking for a beer of his own and was tasting two beers at once in the Oerbar.
- "Now we just need to make a beer, we already have the name."
- A strong, smooth sipping beer, comparable to the Westmalle Tripel of 1936.

### More of our beers

- Oerbier 9%
- Arabier 8%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Boskeun 9% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Stille Nacht
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/stille-nacht

← All beers

12%

Our prestige beer

## Stille Nacht

- 12%
- Christmas beer
- Refermented in the bottle Our prestige beer, with every trump card on the table: 1,000 kg of malt for 2,500 litres of beer, pale candi sugar and whole-cone hops from Poperinge (Whitbread Golding Variety). A very long boil, long lagering and refermentation in the bottle. Good for 22° Plato and 12%. At Christmas it can be a little more!

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Ripe fruit and candi sugar.

Taste
Full and sweetish, carried by the high gravity.

Finish
Warming and long.

In the glass
The poster

#### Serving tip
Pour it slowly into the Oerbier glass or a wine glass, and take your time.

#### Keeping
Stille Nacht ages well. The bottling date is on the crown cap.

#### Where to buy
At the brewery, during Oerbar opening hours (Saturday and Sunday, 2 pm to 7 pm). Also at our points of sale: see the map.

#### Did you know...

- In 1980 there were no Christmas beers in Belgium, apart from six English ones.
- The name Stille Nacht ("Silent Night") came out of a brainstorm with brother Ward. He is the spiritual father of the name.
- Boiled in a copper kettle over a direct gas flame and cooled in the copper coolship from 1921.
- Fermented in open copper fermenters, then matured for at least a month.
- Refermented in the bottle.

### A new Christmas card every year
Every year around Christmas, Benjamin Herteleer draws a new Christmas card with the characters Kris once drew for the labels: the Stille Nacht figure, the Oerbier figure, the Dulle Teve, the Arabier macaw and the Boskeun. Glass in hand, ready for the season's greetings. The new card always appears on @dedollebrouwers .

### The best Christmas beer in Belgium
Every year the beer tasters of OBER in Essen (near Antwerp) hold a festival with nothing but Belgian Christmas beers. Since 1994 the visitors pick their favourite there, out of more than 200 beers. No expert jury: the beers are bought and poured anonymously. Stille Nacht nearly always ends up in the top 3. Since 2005 it has received the certificate for best Christmas beer eleven times, and it already won in the years before that, when no certificates were handed out yet. It also came second or third several times, Stille Nacht Reserva included. The certificates hang in the Oerbar.
In the press: In de Gazette (2025) ↗ · O.B.E.R. (2023) ↗ · Discover Benelux (2018) ↗ · Het Laatste Nieuws (2014) ↗ · Gazet van Antwerpen (2012) ↗ · Het Nieuwsblad (2012) ↗ · Biernet (2012) ↗

# Export Stout
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/export-stout

← All beers

8%

Full-bodied, dark and roasted

## Export Stout

- 8%
- Stout
- Refermented in the bottle Our American importer B. United asked Guinness to brew a stout for them. Guinness refused, and Matthias of B. United asked whether we were interested. That's how we started brewing stout. The first stouts were a variation on Oerbier, with more roasted malt and candi sugar, at 9%. Today it is drier, without candi sugar, and 8%.

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Roasted malt.

Taste
Full and bitter, with dark malt.

Finish
Dry and bitter.

#### When
We brew it only a few times a year. Be quick.

#### Serving tip
Pour at 10-12°C into the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

#### Keeping
Keeps for two years.

#### Did you know...

- Stout used to be a beer the doctor prescribed, for instance when brother Ward had broken his leg.
- Old stout labels said "recommended for invalids": for people getting back on their feet.
- Every batch of stout gets a different recipe. We have a folder full of all the recipes.
- The first labels and posters still say 9%. Today it is 8%.
- The same fermentation as Oerbier.
- It no longer goes to America. Every brewery there now makes its own stout, IPA, bourbon stout, vanilla stout, pastry stout with marshmallows, milkshake stout, and so on, and so on…

### The label
The round stamp on every bottle of Export Stout shows the brewery in Esen, with the brewer's signature. It still says 9%, as strong as the very first stouts. A classic, handmade design, fitting for a beer with just as few frills.

### More of our beers

- Oerbier 9%
- Arabier 8%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Boskeun 9% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Lichtervelds Blond
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/lichtervelds-blond

← All beers

8%

Golden blond, once every two years

## Lichtervelds Blond

- 8%
- Golden blond
- Refermented in the bottle A revived beer from Lichtervelde: originally "Blonde des Flandres" from brewery De Hoop / Th. Labens, now brewed and bottled by De Dolle Brouwers in Esen.

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Soft malt, a hint of citrus and discreet hops.

Taste
Round and full for a blond beer, with a soft sweetness that turns into a drier finish.

Finish
Fairly long and dry, with a subtle warmth from the alcohol.

#### Serving tip
Serve at 8-10°C in the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

#### Goes with
Light lunch dishes, mature cheese or as an aperitif.

#### Did you know...

- Brewed at the request of the local history society Karel Van de Poele in Lichtervelde.
- On the market since 1990, each time for the Lichtervelde folklore festival held every two years.
- Brewed only once every two years.
- Taste, colour and strength vary slightly from batch to batch.
- It has its own glass: a schwenker.

### A revived local beer
The label refers to the original brewery "De Hoop" and maltings of Th. Labens in Lichtervelde (West Flanders), which once brewed this beer as "Blonde des Flandres". De Dolle Brouwers brews and bottles it again today in Esen, in the spirit of the original: pure malt and hops, unfiltered, refermented in the bottle.

### More of our beers

- Oerbier 9%
- Arabier 8%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Boskeun 9% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Oeral
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/oeral

← All beers

6%

Only from the tap

## Oeral

- 6%
- Blond and bitter Oeral is a lighter version of Arabier, so blond and bitter. The name comes from "oer", pure, and "al", for everyone ("alleman"). We only pour it from the keg.
On draught only, not bottled

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Fresh whole-cone hops, just like Arabier.

Taste
Blond and bitter, but lighter than Arabier.

Finish
Dry and refreshing.

#### Serving tip
Only available on draught in the Oerbar. Served fresh.

#### Did you know...

- Oeral has a long and murky history.
- It was first brewed for the first Arabier festival. Because drinking Arabier and water separately is fiction, and Arabier as a main course is a daring undertaking, even for trained beer lovers.
- The label went from a little yellow plane to the Oeral building with hammer and sickle: Oeral as the far edge of Europe (the Urals), and the far edge of the art of beer…
- Oeral doesn't keep long. Alcohol isn't just a cleaning product but also a preservative, and Oeral has less of it.
- It's the only beer in our range that we don't bottle: it's purely for the Oerbar and the tap.

### More of our beers

- Oerbier 9%
- Arabier 8%
- Stille Nacht 12%
- Boskeun 9% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Oerbier Reserva
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/oerbier-reserva

← All beers
9%

Oerbier, aged in wine barrels

## Oerbier Reserva

- 9%
- Dark, barrel-aged
- Refermented in the bottle After twelve months in wine barrels, the dark base of Oerbier picks up notes of wood and wine.
Currently out of stock

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Red fruit, a hint of oak and the malty base of Oerbier.

Taste
Round and complex, with tannin and notes of wood and wine on top of the familiar Oerbier base.

Finish
Long, dry and slightly wine-like.

#### Serving tip
Serve at 12°C in a wine glass, so the wood notes can shine.

#### Goes with
Aged cheese, game or a dark chocolate dessert.

#### Did you know...

- We use wine barrels from France, Spain and Italy, and each barrel only once.
- Every month we top up the barrels, so no air gets to the beer.
- The label says which barrel the beer comes from, for example "barrique 11".
- Store the bottles upright and cool.
- Always a small edition.
- The names Reserva and Gran Reserva come from the wine world, for wine aged in barrels. That's something different from the French Grand Cru.

At least twelve months in oak

### About the barrel ageing
We have been ageing beer in wine barrels since 1996, and since 2000 there have been three Reservas: Oerbier, Dulle Teve and Stille Nacht. That makes De Dolle Brouwers one of the pioneers of barrel-aged beer in Belgium. Now and then a selected batch of Oerbier goes into wine barrels for at least a year, where it develops further and takes on notes of wood, wine and tannin, each time in a limited, numbered edition.

### More Reserva

- Dulle Teve Reserva 10%
- Stille Nacht Reserva 12% Where can I drink this? Or come and taste it in Esen

# Dulle Teve Reserva
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/dulle-teve-reserva

← All beers
10%

Dulle Teve, aged in wine barrels

## Dulle Teve Reserva

- 10%
- Tripel, barrel-aged
- Refermented in the bottle Extra round and warming: the tannins of the wine barrel add weight to the already sturdy Dulle Teve.
Currently out of stock

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Dark fruit, a hint of oak and the spicy kick of Dulle Teve.

Taste
Full and complex, with notes of wood and wine that soften the base.

Finish
Long, dry and slightly tannic.

#### Serving tip
Serve at 12°C in the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass and give it time to open up.

#### Goes with
Game, hearty stews or a sharp hard cheese.

#### Did you know...

- We use wine barrels from France, Spain and Italy, and each barrel only once.
- Every month we top up the barrels, so no air gets to the beer.
- The label says which barrel the beer comes from, for example "barrique 11".
- Store the bottles upright and cool.
- The names Reserva and Gran Reserva come from the wine world, for wine aged in barrels. That's something different from the French Grand Cru.

At least twelve months in oak

### About the barrel ageing
Since 2000, now and then a selected batch of Dulle Teve also goes into wine barrels for at least a year. The tannins and wood notes give the beer an extra layer of complexity, each time in a limited, numbered edition.

# Stille Nacht Reserva
Source: https://www.dedollebrouwers.be/en/beers/stille-nacht-reserva

← All beers
12%

Stille Nacht, aged for years in wine barrels

## Stille Nacht Reserva

- 12%
- Golden, barrel-aged
- Refermented in the bottle The complex, golden Stille Nacht gets a second life here: about two years in barrels that used to hold wine, into a deeper, woodier and slightly vinous beer of 12%. Not a yearly edition but a release every few years, each with its own barrel number.
75 cl sold out, 33 cl still available

### Tasting notes
Aroma
Oak, vanilla, dried fruit, citrus peel and a hint of wild yeast.

Taste
Lightly sour and fruity, with candied orange, wood and a soft vinous touch that trades the original Stille Nacht sweetness for more depth.

Finish
Long and warming, with the high strength well hidden behind wood and fruit.

#### Serving tip
Serve at 12°C in a wine glass — a bottle is meant for sharing on a special occasion.

#### Goes with
Aged cheese, a fruit dessert or simply on its own, to finish.

#### Did you know...

- We use wine barrels from France, Spain and Italy, and each barrel only once.
- Every month we top up the barrels, so no air gets to the beer.
- The label says which barrel the beer comes from, for example "barrique 11".
- Store the bottles upright and cool.
- The year on a Reserva refers to the year the beer was brewed, not the bottling date.
- The names Reserva and Gran Reserva come from the wine world, for wine aged in barrels. That's something different from the French Grand Cru.

Kris tasting from the barrel

### About the barrel ageing
Stille Nacht Reserva was our very first Reserva, and it started with a little accident. With Stille Nacht 2000 the yeast mutated during the refermentation in the bottle. The beer hadn't finished fermenting and the bottles exploded. So we poured the beer into empty 225-litre Bordeaux barrels, where it aged for two years. Then it was refermented in 75 cl bottles. Today Stille Nacht Reserva is not a yearly release: every few years a selected batch goes into wine barrels for at least two years, before it is bottled as a numbered Reserva (per "barrique"). The bottles are limited and mostly sold directly at the brewery.
